Where we work: two crews, seven counties

Opera Concrete & Pavers runs two crews on opposite sides of Florida. The Kissimmee & Greater Orlando crew covers Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Lake and Polk counties; the Sarasota crew covers Sarasota and Manatee counties. As of November 2026 each has its own phone line and free on-site estimates.

Which crew to call

Kissimmee & Greater Orlando

Based in Kissimmee. Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Lake and Polk counties. Phone: (689) 354-0025.

Sarasota, Lakewood Ranch & Bradenton

Based in Sarasota. Sarasota and Manatee counties. Phone: (941) 207-7585.

The rule of thumb is the county your property sits in, not the distance from where a crew is based. Look up the county on your tax bill or property appraiser record if you're unsure, and call the crew that lists it. Neither crew's list overlaps the other's: no county appears on both.

Where the line falls

The split follows county lines. On the Central Florida side the crew starts in Orange County (Orlando, Winter Garden, Windermere, Apopka), takes in Osceola (Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Celebration, Poinciana), Seminole (Oviedo, Sanford, Lake Mary), Lake (Clermont, Minneola, Groveland) and Polk, where the town on our list is Davenport. On the Gulf side the crew works Manatee (Bradenton, Palmetto, Parrish) and Sarasota (Sarasota, Venice, North Port).

Lakewood Ranch is the one place where a single community crosses a county line, with homes in both Manatee and Sarasota. It belongs to the Sarasota crew either way. Counties that sit between or beside the two regions, such as Hillsborough and Charlotte, aren't on either crew's list; the last section below says what to do if your property is there.

How the two coasts differ

The same installation steps apply on both sides, but the ground and the rules around it don't match. The table sums up the differences that change a quote.

Central Florida versus the Suncoast
FactorKissimmee & Greater OrlandoSarasota, Lakewood Ranch & Bradenton
SoilExcessively drained ridge sand in Lake County; flatwoods through Orlando and KissimmeeFlatwoods sand almost everywhere, with groundwater often within 6 to 18 inches
Annual rainfall (NOAA 1991–2020)51.45 in. at Orlando International49.05 in. at Sarasota–Bradenton airport
Salt air and flood zonesNot a factor inlandGulf and bay shoreline, FEMA zones AE and VE, a state setback line on the beaches
Watering orders, 2026St. Johns River district schedule; Lake County under a tighter orderSouthwest Florida district once-a-week order through March 31, 2027
HOA densityBaldwin Park, Lake Nona, Celebration and many village boardsLakewood Ranch villages, Palmer Ranch, Venetian Golf & River Club

Soil and rainfall figures are explained, with sources, on each crew's own page.

Soil series and flood zones are cited on the Kissimmee & Greater Orlando page and the Sarasota page. The ICPI paver guide adds 2 to 4 inches of base on wet soils, which is why a Lakewood Ranch paver base is often deeper than one in Clermont (ICPI Tech Spec 2). Rainfall figures come from NOAA's normals (NOAA 1991–2020 normals).

What both crews do

The services are the same on both sides, in this order of emphasis: paver driveways, patios and pool decks; paver sealing and paver restoration; then concrete driveways, other flatwork, artificial turf and retaining walls. Prices are market ranges on the cost pages, and the permits and HOA hub lists who handles approvals in each county. The sequence from visit to walkthrough is on the process page.

Do you work outside these towns?

Possibly. The lists below are the towns each crew has a page for, not a fence. If your property is in a nearby town or county that isn't listed, ask: call the crew closest to you ((689) 354-0025 for Central Florida, (941) 207-7585 for the Suncoast) or describe the address in the estimate form, and the answer comes back before anyone books a visit.
